# Pre-Implementation Checklist: Release Notes & PR Summary Generation

**Purpose**: A solo, standard-depth requirements-quality gate covering the three areas with the most implementation risk if left ambiguous — security/secrets handling, cost transparency & release immutability, and the CLI contract — reviewed before `/speckit-implement` writes any code.
**Created**: 2026-09-12
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md), [plan.md](../plan.md), [contracts/cli-interface.md](../contracts/cli-interface.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Security & Secrets Handling Requirements

- [ ] CHK001 Is the exact set of required credentials (`GITHUB_TOKEN`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`) and their required permission scope explicitly documented for both read-only and `--publish` scenarios? [Completeness, Spec §Assumptions, contracts/cli-interface.md Configuration contract]
- [ ] CHK002 Is an "invalid" credential distinguished from a "missing" one, with distinct error-message content specified for each? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK003 Is the requirement that credentials MUST NOT be persisted or exposed (FR-009) precise enough to be testable — e.g. does it cover partial/masked token fragments, not just full raw values? [Measurability, Spec §FR-009]
- [ ] CHK004 Is it specified whether `GITHUB_TOKEN` needs elevated (write/release) scope only when `--publish` is used, or whether a single scope is assumed for every run? [Ambiguity, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK005 Are the "never expose credentials in generated files" requirement (FR-009) and the Usage Record / cost-log schema — itself a generated file — consistent with each other? [Consistency, Spec §FR-009, data-model.md Usage Record]
- [ ] CHK006 Does the spec define behavior when the GitHub token can read but lacks release-creation permission specifically during a `--publish` run, as distinct from the token being entirely invalid? [Gap, Edge Case]

## Cost Transparency & Release Immutability Requirements

- [x] CHK007 Is "a small, fixed number of times with backoff" (FR-014) quantified with an actual retry count and backoff schedule, or left to implementation discretion? [Clarity, Spec §FR-014] — Resolved 2026-09-12: FR-014 now specifies 3 attempts total, exponential backoff from 2s.
- [ ] CHK008 Is the pricing table's source and update mechanism specified — who updates it and how staleness would be noticed — given research.md notes the price is hardcoded? [Gap, research.md "Cost calculation"]
- [ ] CHK009 Are the units and rounding rules for `estimated_cost_usd` specified, so two independent implementations would compute the same displayed value? [Measurability, data-model.md Usage Record]
- [ ] CHK010 Is the criterion for "notes already exist for a release" (FR-012) fully unambiguous — does a release in any state (draft, published, or a deleted-then-recreated tag) count as "existing"? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-012, Clarifications]
- [x] CHK011 Are "the local file is still written" (spec Clarifications) and FR-012's "MUST NOT regenerate... notes for that release" consistent — is "regenerate" scoped only to the published release, or could a reader take it to also block the local file? [Consistency, Spec Clarifications vs. FR-012] — Resolved 2026-09-12: FR-012 now states explicitly that immutability applies only to the published release; the local file always regenerates.
- [ ] CHK012 Is behavior specified for the local file differing between two runs of the same release/window (e.g. due to AI output variability) while the published release itself stays immutable? [Gap, Edge Case]
- [ ] CHK013 Are all four Release Identity fields (release name, version, RC branch, commit SHA) each given a clear derivation/source rule, or only `version`'s? [Completeness, data-model.md Release Identity]

## CLI Contract & Error Handling Requirements

- [ ] CHK014 Is the full set of mutually-exclusive/required flag combinations enumerated — e.g. is `--from-ref` supplied without `--to-ref` addressed as clearly as "both date and ref options together"? [Completeness, contracts/cli-interface.md]
- [ ] CHK015 Is the content of a "clear, actionable error message" (FR-008) specified beyond the word "clear" — e.g. must it name the specific missing variable? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK016 Is exit code 1 further differentiated across its several listed causes (bad credentials, AI failure, PR-cap exceeded, invalid ref), or must a caller distinguish them only by parsing error text? [Ambiguity, contracts/cli-interface.md Exit codes]
- [ ] CHK017 Are requirements defined for what the CLI reports when the PR-volume soft cap (FR-017) is exceeded — e.g. is the actual count surfaced, or only a generic error? [Gap, Spec §FR-017]
- [ ] CHK018 Are the "notes already exist" success path (exit 0) and the several exit-code-1 failure paths consistently scoped for what does/doesn't get written to disk, leaving no combination undefined? [Consistency, contracts/cli-interface.md File output contract]
- [x] CHK019 Are recovery requirements defined for a run that fails after the local file is written but before a requested publish completes (a partial success across the two outputs)? [Gap, Exception Flow] — Resolved 2026-09-12: new FR-018 defines this case explicitly (local file kept, clear distinguishing error, no partial release).

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify` — this file is independent of that one.
- Items are numbered sequentially (CHK001-CHK019) for easy reference.
